notes:
Summary: mid-market SaaS (customer engagement) evaluating Redwood for live chat and reranking/embeddings. Strong GDPR/data residency constraint — legal insists user data, context windows stored and processed in EU-only region. Started with hosted_api POC in eu-west-1 (Ireland) to evaluate latency and cost. Observations: avg p95 token latency ~120-160ms for Dublin users (good), but users in Germany/Poland see 220-320ms under sustained load (30 rps simulated) — likely routing through non-optimal edge / AZs. Customer asks about multi-region routing that keeps data in EU (e.g., route FR/DE traffic to eu-central while keeping all logs & KV cache in EU tenancy).

POC details:
- Workload: 30 rps chat peak, 50k tokens/day, embeddings for search daily batch, reranking inline for top-5 candidates.
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for chat (soft), p50 <= 120ms.
- Cost sensitivity: target net cost <= current in-house GPU infra spend; open to committed Dedicated if unit economics break-even.
- Compliance: must have EU data residency for processing & retention; retention controls required (ability to TTL or opt-out logs), audit logging and KMS integration.

Conversations so far: notes from demo — "Flow looked great, but we can't accept US fallback for any user data; need EU-only fallback policies." (quote from CTO). Product team asked about warm KV cache replication across EU regions and the operational complexity. SE (Jonah) proposed two options: 1) Hosted in single EU region + autoscale with lower latency for most users; 2) Dedicated pools deployed in eu-central-1 with multi-AZ and optional replica read endpoints in eu-west-1 for geographic optimization.

Security: submitted questionnaire; requested Redwood SOC2 + ISO docs and contact for legal to finalize DPA with EU residency clause. Jira SEC-4187 open for legal clarifications.

Next steps:
- Deliver POC perf report by 2026-03-12 (Jonah) including latency heatmap by country & routing trace samples.
- Pricing sheet for Dedicated EU reserved 3-month trial and 12-month commit (Maya).
- Legal to review DPA draft (Aurora legal team) and confirm whether mirror/fallback endpoints outside EU are allowed for non-PII data (blocker).

Other notes: They mentioned competitor evaluations (Anthropic + cloud-managed endpoints). Aurora likes Redwood's unified runtime and routing policy ideas but price sensitive. Short timeline: procurement decision targeted Apr 2026.
